key_insight: Tool rankings alone are not enough for LLM agents—CAM-DF learns when to stop acquiring tools by balancing expected utility against heterogeneous acquisition costs.
engineering_relevance: This gives agent builders a lightweight pre-execution control layer that can reduce tool overhead, context load, and privacy exposure without changing the underlying LLM.
method: Formulate tool acquisition as cost-aware marginal decision-focused stopping over ranked tool prefixes.
Train on the offline gap between stopping now and the best continuation, using the gap sign for the decision and its magnitude as the loss weight.
Use CAM-DF-lite as a compact, interpretable variant for deployment.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 1,343 tasks across five tool-use domains, CAM-DF achieved the highest payoff on τ-bench Retail and exposed the agent to 37% fewer tools in live execution while maintaining comparable task success.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the ranking source and the assumed cost regime, so deployment should validate the stopping rule under the target tool-cost distribution.
paper_title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
